Why did WWII soldiers tape two ammunition magazines together? The trick, common in the Pacific Theater with weapons like the Thompson submachine gun and M1 carbine, let soldiers eject an empty mag, flip the taped pair, and instantly load a fresh one — no reaching for a pouch mid-firefight. Though officially discouraged due to added weight and dirt exposure, the speed advantage made it a popular unofficial field tactic. Learn the real combat history behind this classic duct tape hack.
